sources: Commercial Business Process Lifecycle slide (stages 1-3, processes a-l)
Industry grounding: ETRM front/middle/back office lifecycle; downstream commercial value chain (trading & supply, planning & optimization, marketing/pricing/retail)

name: Commercial Hydrocarbon Lifecycle
description: End-to-end commercial lifecycle for hydrocarbon supply, trading, logistics, channel sales, and control: market intelligence through deal execution, physical operations, pricing/retail, risk, settlement, and backcasting.
trigger: Market/supply opportunity informed by strategic supply & demand plan
outcome: Profitable placement of crude/products with controlled risk, settled transactions, and learnings fed back to planning

capabilities.name: Market Intelligence
capabilities.description: Monitor and interpret market data, competitor actions, and internal performance to inform commercial decisions.

capabilities.name: Price Management
capabilities.description: Transform market data and internal assessment into validated price systems of record.

capabilities.name: Supply & Trading Strategy
capabilities.description: Devise procurement and trading strategy: which crude grades/products to buy and sell, in what quantities.

capabilities.name: Deal Capture & Contracting
capabilities.description: Negotiate and execute deals with counterparties; capture trades and contracts.

capabilities.name: Logistics Planning & Scheduling
capabilities.description: Nominate and schedule physical movement of crude and products from seller to buyer.

capabilities.name: Terminal & Transport Execution
capabilities.description: Execute planned physical movement and bulk loading safely and efficiently.

capabilities.name: Product Quality & Loss Management
capabilities.description: Assess product quality via assay/lab data; manage custody transfer gains/losses.

capabilities.name: Channel Pricing & Sales
capabilities.description: Set wholesale rack prices and execute final sale to end consumers at branded retail.

capabilities.name: Commercial Risk & Position Management
capabilities.description: EOD valuation of positions against closing prices; official daily P&L, VaR, and risk metrics.

capabilities.name: Settlement & Reconciliation
capabilities.description: Finalize financial aspects of wholesale and retail transactions; allocate costs; manage claims from physical discrepancies.

capabilities.name: Performance Management & Backcasting
capabilities.description: Compare actuals against perfect-foresight optimum; quantify value leakage; identify root causes for improvement.

capabilities.name: Planning & Optimization
capabilities.description: Cross-stage value chain planning and optimization capability; owns the Planning & Optimization data product line.

stages.name: Market & Strategy Formation
stages.description: From market monitoring to executed deals.

processes.name: Market Intelligence & Planning
processes.description: Continuously monitor real-time market data, competitor actions, and internal sales performance; informed by the strategic supply & demand plan, forming the tactical foundation for daily commercial decisions.
processes.rationale: Consumes market feeds, plan context (whole P&O line), and margin signal; does not own a trade or price system of record.

processes.name: Market Price Calculation & Validation
processes.description: Transform raw market data and internal price assessment into official, validated system of record for all product prices.
processes.rationale: Classic price SoR publish (market operations): owns Master Pricing; consumes market feeds and deal context.

processes.name: Supply & Procurement Strategy
processes.description: Based on market analysis and refinery needs, traders devise a procurement strategy: which crude grades/finished product to buy, in what quantities.
processes.rationale: Strategy formation needs current positions, risk appetite/limits, and the planning/optimization line.

processes.name: Deal Negotiation & Capture
processes.description: Traders engage counterparties to execute the deal: bilateral (phone/chat), through brokers, or on electronic platforms.
processes.rationale: Front-office deal capture owns the trade facts (Physical Trading); constrained by risk limits and validated price curves.

stages.name: Execution & Operations
stages.description: Physical movement, quality, wholesale and retail execution.

processes.name: Logistics Planning & Scheduling
processes.description: Focus shifts to physically moving the crude; schedulers/logistics coordinators work with traders to nominate and schedule transport from seller to buyer.
processes.rationale: Schedulers nominate against trades and plan and own the logistics execution data.

processes.name: Terminal & Transport Operations
processes.description: Execute the planned physical movement and loading of bulk product safely and efficiently.
processes.rationale: Physical execution produces movement actuals (Logistic Execution); custody-transfer loss and quality data are critical operating inputs.

processes.name: Quality Assessment & Blending Ops
processes.description: Traders use lab data to assess crude quality, from assay data at loading or internal lab samples on receipt.
processes.rationale: Lab/assay operations own the Quality Assurance product; parcel/cargo context and loss data consumed.

processes.name: Rack Price Setting
processes.description: Calculate, approve, and publish competitive and profitable wholesale rack prices for the next sales cycle.
processes.rationale: Wholesale rack publish informed by the master price SoR and margin targets.

processes.name: Retail Sales & Payment
processes.description: Execute the final sale to the end consumer at branded retail sites, securely process payments, and capture granular transaction data.
processes.rationale: Channel sales/payment capture owns Retail Payments; rack price is the critical input.

stages.name: Risk, Performance, and Control
stages.description: Risk, settlement, and performance feedback into the next cycle.

processes.name: Risk Management and Position Monitoring
processes.description: Runs in parallel to trading and scheduling: official EOD valuation of all positions against closing market prices; calculate and validate official daily P&L, VaR, and key risk metrics.
processes.rationale: Middle office owns the Commercial Risk product (positions, P&L, VaR) computed from trades and validated prices.

processes.name: Performance Tracking & Analysis
processes.description: Track financial and operational performance of trades; through backcasting, compare actual results against the perfect-foresight optimum to quantify value leakage and identify root causes.
processes.rationale: Backcasting owns the Backcasting & Refining CI product; consumes margin outcomes and the planning line as baseline.

processes.name: Settlement and Post-Trade Reconciliation
processes.description: Finalize all financial aspects of wholesale and retail transactions, accurately allocate costs, and manage claims arising from physical discrepancies.
processes.rationale: Back office settles trades against price SoRs and risk data. Loss Control and Retail Payments enter via claims/retail settlement.

flows.note: Loops back to Market Intelligence & Planning
Backcast learnings feed next planning cycle

gapAnalysis.note: LSC covers loyalty/cards administration; granular retail transaction capture and payment processing are not decomposed.
No dedicated custody-transfer/loss-control process nodes; data portfolio exists without a clear LSC owner process.
Quality management exists; blending operations may span Refining (L1 stub, not decomposed).
